record.paper_title: Monetary Stabilization in Cryptocurrencies—Design Approaches and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Self-tokenizing open market operations under stress
record.original_question: In stablecoins that contract supply through self-tokenizing open market operations—creating special-purpose internal tokens, selling them for stablecoins, and destroying the acquired stablecoins—how resilient is the mechanism when demand falls or speculative attacks repeat, given that buyers of special-purpose tokens must be compensated with future minted money or future money-growth ownership?

evidence.quote:
Self-tokenizing OMO decreases supply not by selling ex-
ternal assets, but other assets generated within their own
ecosystem. Examples are Basecoin [3], Carbon [37] and
Fragments [38]. All these projects target a 1-to-1 relationship
between their stablecoin and the USD. To decrease the money
supply, the projects propose mechanisms that create special-
purpose tokens that are sold for stablecoins which are then
destroyed by the system. In theory, with such a design, supply
can be decreased to any desired level. This is different from
standard and proxy OMO that are restricted by the available
reserves of external assets. In practice, many open questions
remain (addressed in Sec. V).

In self-tokenizing OMO not reserves but special-purpose
tokens are sold against currency units. While the designs of
the tokens vary, all provide some form of success-related
monetary incentive that is payed out if a certain target price
for the stablecoin is achieved. The incentive is paid out in
form of newly minted money supply. The lower the prob-
ability of success, the higher the necessary incentives. Risk
is either remunerated by higher relative ownership of future
money growth or by a promised absolute increase of future
minted money. Excessive use thus may either lead to reduced
ownership in risk remuneration or to an uncontrolled increase
of promises of future remuneration in the money supply.

While in the presence of speculators for and against the peg
the ﬁrst series of speculative attacks might be neutralized,
claims for risk remuneration will stack up quickly. Leading to
a decrease in relative ownership of future remuneration, this
will decrease the demand for the used special-purpose tokens
with every round of attack. Missing demand for the self-issued
tokens makes it impossible to absorb money supply and defend
against the attack. Further research is strongly encouraged as
the above setup is quite popular. Nine out of the 24 reviewed
projects and thus almost 38 % consider it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a stablecoin system that targets a fixed peg (e.g., 1 unit of stablecoin = 1 USD) and that contracts its circulating money supply via a "self-tokenizing" open market operation defined as follows. When the stablecoin price falls below the peg, the system issues special-purpose internal tokens (distinct from the stablecoin) and auctions them for stablecoins; the stablecoins received are then destroyed (burned). Holders of the special-purpose tokens are entitled to a future payoff, paid only when the stablecoin returns to and remains at the peg, in one of two forms:

(a) a promised absolute quantity of newly minted future stablecoins (debt-like claim), or
(b) a relative share of all future money-supply growth (equity-like claim).

Let demand for the stablecoin follow a stochastic process subject to negative shocks and to repeated speculative attacks against the peg. Each contraction round increases the outstanding stock of unredeemed special-purpose token claims, which in turn dilutes the per-token expected payoff (under scheme (b)) or expands the contingent future supply obligation (under scheme (a)).

Formulate and analyze a model of this mechanism that answers the following:

1. Derive conditions on the demand process, attack frequency, and risk-adjusted discount factor of speculators under which there exists a market-clearing price for the special-purpose tokens that allows the system to absorb a given contraction in stablecoin supply.

2. Determine whether, under repeated speculative attacks, the sequence of clearing prices for special-purpose tokens converges to zero in finite time (mechanism failure) or remains bounded away from zero (mechanism resilience), and characterize the threshold separating these regimes for both compensation schemes (a) and (b).

3. Compare schemes (a) and (b): show whether one is strictly more resilient than the other, or identify parameter regions in which each dominates.

Provide either an existence/stability theorem for the peg-defense mechanism or a proof that no such mechanism can sustain the peg almost surely against an adversary capable of arbitrarily many attack rounds.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether self-tokenizing (seigniorage-share / bond-style) stablecoin contractions are robust to repeated speculative attacks and prolonged demand declines remains an open and actively debated research question. Empirical failures of such designs (e.g., the collapse of Basis Cash and the May 2022 collapse of Terra/UST, which used a related two-token absorption mechanism) are widely cited as evidence that the mechanism is fragile, and several theoretical analyses (e.g., on "death spirals" of algorithmic stablecoins) provide partial negative results, but no general resilience theorem or full characterization is established.

status_evidence.title: Terra Money: Stability and Adoption / collapse analyses
status_evidence.snippet: Terra's algorithmic stablecoin UST de-pegged in May 2022 amid speculative pressure; the absorption mechanism via the LUNA token failed as LUNA supply hyperinflated.
status_evidence.claim: Real-world self-tokenizing-style stablecoin mechanisms have failed under attack, illustrating that resilience is not guaranteed.

status_evidence.title: On the instability of bitcoin without the blockchain / Algorithmic stablecoin death spirals (survey literature)
status_evidence.snippet: Analyses of algorithmic stablecoins describe death-spiral dynamics where compensation tokens lose value during attacks, undermining the contraction mechanism.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical work provides partial negative results but no complete resilience characterization.
